note: Phase M1 scenario evidence for vendored Elisp packages (master plan 2026-08-21, section 5). Each package names its tracked source with provenance and a SHA256, the result of loading it unmodified, the features it requires and whether kg advertises them, the scenarios that pin its behaviour by input domain, and the domains it excludes with the scenario or feature id that records the gap. The four labels from section 3.1 are kept distinct: only scenario-green and supported are product claims. Snapshots in oracle/ are generated by `make package-oracle' against the pinned Emacs; the check (`make package-compat-check') regenerates nothing. A scenario pins an exact value, an exact condition, or a deliberately recorded divergence -- never a prose 'loads' or 'is supported' claim. Where kg answers wrongly today, the divergence is RECORDED here, not fixed: that is M2's job.

packages.name: s.el

required_features.note: (provide 's) is reached on load and featurep returns t, so the name is honestly advertised; that is the whole of what this label claims -- the supported contract is not complete (see exclusions and support_label).

packages.support_label_rationale: Unmodified s.el loads and a wide band of entry points completes without a raise (trim, collapse, split, join, lines, prefix/suffix/contains, literal replacement, aget formatting, match, count-matches, repeat, ASCII capitalize/titleize, exact-condition captures, s-lex-format value expansion, and s-format-resolve all agree with the pinned Emacs). It is NOT scenario-green because non-ASCII case folding still diverges (s-upcase-utf8); 'smoke-green' is the honest top label, not a support claim.

known_exclusions.reason: kg case-folds ASCII-only; non-ASCII codepoints are left unchanged, so (s-upcase "café") returns "CAFé" where Emacs returns "CAFÉ". Recorded as a divergence, not fixed (M2).
